There are 43 children diagnosed with cancer every day, and 5 of those 43 will not survive. Investments in research through financial donations from Wren’s Village drive advancements in pediatric cancer treatment, while our family support endeavors make a difference in the lives of those impacted by childhood cancer.

Issue: 1 in 3 families with a child in active cancer treatment are unable to afford basic needs.Action: Wren’s Wallets are filled with $250 in gift cards to help with gas, medicine, food, some fun, and a lot of hope.Impact: These wallets, stuffed by Wren herself, with some help from friends, ease the unexpected financial costs and burden of pediatric cancer on a family, regardless of where they are in their journey – new diagnosis, unexpected hospital admission, relapse, or end of life care.

Issue: When Wren needed blood for her treatments, there was a critical shortage.Action: With community support, Wren’s mother hosted the first #AllinForWren blood drive in Wren’s honor a few weeks after her diagnosis in 2016. Over 200 people showed up to donate. This was the first of many blood drives sparking awareness into Action. Each unit of blood goes on to save up to 3 lives.Impact: 60% of the 200 people at the first #AllinForWren blood drive were first-time donors who now donate annually. Wren’s Village continues to host blood drives every year. The 8th annual #ALLinForWren blood drive was held on September 8, 2023. 104 units of blood were collected along with the 1000th unit of blood donated since the beginning of #AllinForWren blood drives. Wren’s mom had the honor of donating the 1000th unit in Wren's honor.

Bloodmobiles, or mobile blood donation centers, enable blood to be donated from anywhere. Rather than hosting a drive that requires donors to come to the Red Cross, bloodmobiles can be parked at churches, colleges, office buildings and local community centers to draw higher numbers of donors.The newest bloodmobile added to our local Red Cross fleet was fundraised and paid for in Wren’s and pediatric cancer warriors’ honor. With four private donor rooms, state-of-the-art equipment and enhanced air filtration systems, more “unicorn juice” donations can be collected safely and efficiently. Every 2 seconds someone in the U.S. needs blood and or platelets, not just children with cancer. Thanks to generous donors, blood was available when Wren needed it most. Wren says “Let’s roll up our sleeves, restock the hospital shelves, and make a profound impact on the lives of kids just like me, locally and across the country.”

Issue: Funding for pediatric cancer research totals less than 4% on a national level.Action: In September 2016, right after Wren’s diagnosis, a group of neighbors in Wren’s neighborhood of Baxter Village hiked 12 miles in support of a fundraiser sponsored by Harlan’s Heroes for CureSearch, which aims to end childhood cancer with accelerated and innovative research initiatives. This was the genesis of the name “Wren’s Village.”In 2021, Brandi was nominated as a candidate for Woman of the Year by The Leukemia and Lymphoma Society, a philanthropic fundraising competition. With the support of Wren’s Village behind her, she was able to raise $355,000 in 10 weeks. She was runner-up in the Charlotte region and Top 10 nationally. In addition, Wren’s Village has supported the Keep Pounding initiative at Levine Children’s Hospital and Levine Cancer Institute, which treats child and adult patients via their 5K and virtual fundraising campaigns. Wren’s Village has also encouraged support to the following local foundations and non-profit organizations: Red Cross of the Greater Carolinas, the Isabella Santos Foundation, Camp Care, and Claire’s Army.Wren’s Village is registered and verified with Guidestar, Benevity, YourCause, and Network for Good to receive and make donations to pediatric cancer treatment research centers and trials.Impact: Wren’s neighbors continue to hike, adding more members each year. They also started hosting Wren’s Week fundraising activities, ultimately raising $100,000 through 2020. For every $50,000 raised by Brandi and Wren’s Village for the Leukemia and Lymphoma Society in 2021, a research grant was named in a child’s honor to pediatric cancer-specific research trials. Brandi chose to name $100k each for Mikey and Lily, plus $50k each for Jennings Palmer and Wren Jansen.

Over $87,500 in wallet sponsorships received, allowing Wren’s Village to support more than 350 families undergoing treatment

Over 1000 units of blood donated at Annual Wren’s Blood Drive for transfusions, providing “unicorn juice” to make other children feel better. Countless units are donated

Since Wren’s diagnosis in 2016, over $500,000 has been donated to pediatric cancer treatment research and supporting families

Our Impact

There are 43 children diagnosed with cancer every day, and 5 of those 43 will not survive. Investments in research through financial donations from Wren’s Village drive advancements in pediatric cancer treatment, while our family support endeavors make a difference in the lives of those impacted by childhood cancer.

Taking Care of Families

Issue: 1 in 3 families with a child in active cancer treatment are unable to afford basic needs.

Action: Wren’s Wallets are filled with $250 in gift cards to help with gas, medicine, food, some fun, and a lot of hope.

Impact: These wallets, stuffed by Wren herself, with some help from friends, ease the unexpected financial costs and burden of pediatric cancer on a family, regardless of where they are in their journey – new diagnosis, unexpected hospital admission, relapse, or end of life care.

Blood Donations from Our Village

Issue: When Wren needed blood for her treatments, there was a critical shortage.

Action: With community support, Wren’s mother hosted the first #AllinForWren blood drive in Wren’s honor a few weeks after her diagnosis in 2016. Over 200 people showed up to donate. This was the first of many blood drives sparking awareness into Action. Each unit of blood goes on to save up to 3 lives.

Impact: 60% of the 200 people at the first #AllinForWren blood drive were first-time donors who now donate annually. 

Wren’s Village continues to host blood drives every year. The 8th annual #ALLinForWren blood drive was held on September 8, 2023. 104 units of blood were collected along with the 1000th unit of blood donated since the beginning of #AllinForWren blood drives. Wren’s mom had the honor of donating the 1000th unit in Wren's honor. 


Wren’s Bloodmobile

Bloodmobiles, or mobile blood donation centers, enable blood to be donated from anywhere. Rather than hosting a drive that requires donors to come to the Red Cross, bloodmobiles can be parked at churches, colleges, office buildings and local community centers to draw higher numbers of donors.

The newest bloodmobile added to our local Red Cross fleet was fundraised and paid for in Wren’s and pediatric cancer warriors’ honor. With four private donor rooms, state-of-the-art equipment and enhanced air filtration systems, more “unicorn juice” donations can be collected safely and efficiently. Every 2 seconds someone in the U.S. needs blood and or platelets, not just children with cancer. Thanks to generous donors, blood was available when Wren needed it most. Wren says “Let’s roll up our sleeves, restock the hospital shelves, and make a profound impact on the lives of kids just like me, locally and across the country.”


Funding Pediatric Cancer Research

Issue: Funding for pediatric cancer research totals less than 4% on a national level.

Action: In September 2016, right after Wren’s diagnosis, a group of neighbors in Wren’s neighborhood of Baxter Village hiked 12 miles in support of a fundraiser sponsored by Harlan’s Heroes for CureSearch, which aims to end childhood cancer with accelerated and innovative research initiatives. This was the genesis of the name “Wren’s Village.”

In 2021, Brandi was nominated as a candidate for Woman of the Year by The Leukemia and Lymphoma Society, a philanthropic fundraising competition. With the support of Wren’s Village behind her, she was able to raise $355,000 in 10 weeks. She was runner-up in the Charlotte region and Top 10 nationally. 

In addition, Wren’s Village has supported the Keep Pounding initiative at Levine Children’s Hospital and Levine Cancer Institute, which treats child and adult patients via their 5K and virtual fundraising campaigns. Wren’s Village has also encouraged support to the following local foundations and non-profit organizations: Red Cross of the Greater Carolinas, the Isabella Santos Foundation, Camp Care, and Claire’s Army.

Wren’s Village is registered and verified with Guidestar, Benevity, YourCause, and Network for Good to receive and make donations to pediatric cancer treatment research centers and trials.

Impact: Wren’s neighbors continue to hike, adding more members each year. They also started hosting Wren’s Week fundraising activities, ultimately raising $100,000 through 2020. 

For every $50,000 raised by Brandi and Wren’s Village for the Leukemia and Lymphoma Society in 2021, a research grant was named in a child’s honor to pediatric cancer-specific research trials. Brandi chose to name $100k each for Mikey and Lily, plus $50k each for Jennings Palmer and Wren Jansen. 



Success Stories

Over $87,500 in wallet sponsorships received, allowing Wren’s Village to support more than 350 families undergoing treatment 

Over 1000 units of blood donated at Annual Wren’s Blood Drive for transfusions, providing “unicorn juice” to make other children feel better. Countless units are donated 

Since Wren’s diagnosis in 2016, over $500,000 has been donated to pediatric cancer treatment research and supporting families
